exercise.title: Major 3rd or minor 3rd
exercise.why: A major chord starts with a major 3rd and a minor chord with a minor 3rd, so the sound you already know from chords tells the two 3rds apart.

cells.text:
Press Start in the game below. The game plays two notes, one after the other: pick M3 for a major 3rd, m3 for a minor 3rd, P5 for a 5th or P8 for an octave.
Sort wide from narrow first: the two 3rds are the narrow ones. Then hear the pair as the first two notes of a chord, and ask whether that chord is major or minor.
Practice until you name a 3rd without pressing Replay.
